overview: Hansoh Pharmaceutical is a leading innovation-driven Chinese pharmaceutical group focused on oncology, metabolism, immunology, CNS and anti-infective therapeutic areas, with seven innovative medicines now generating product sales in China and a pipeline of 40+ innovative drug candidates (including multiple ADCs) in over 70 clinical trials. The business is shifting from a generics/licensed-in-China model toward an innovation-and-global-licensing model: innovative medicines and collaboration income reached approximately 82% of FY2025 revenue, and the Group has signed a string of major ex-China out-licensing deals with GSK, Regeneron, Roche and others. Hansoh is Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed (RMB-reporting), with R&D centers in Shanghai, Changzhou, Lianyungang (China) and Maryland (US), and manufacturing/commercialization concentrated in China.

business_model.summary: Revenue is generated primarily from direct sales of pharmaceutical products in China (oncology, anti-infective, CNS and metabolic innovative medicines plus legacy generics), supplemented by a fast-growing stream of upfront payments, milestones and royalties from out-licensing self-developed drug candidates (mainly ADCs and other biologics) to global pharma partners such as GSK, Regeneron, Roche, Hengrui, Glenmark and Avere. The financial-parser identified collaboration/licensing income of approximately RMB2.1 billion in FY2025, embedded within total revenue of RMB15.0 billion and/or other income; this is a newer, higher-margin, deal-based (lumpy) revenue stream layered on top of recurring product sales. Core drug sales are largely recurring/reimbursement-driven (National Reimbursement Drug List inclusion anchors volumes), while licensing income is transactional and milestone-dependent.

revenue_streams.name: Innovative medicines - Oncology (Ameile/aumolertinib, Hansoh Xinfu, Pulaile, Pulaitan, Xinwei)
Innovative medicines - Metabolic/other (Fulaimei, Saint Luolai, Fulaidi, Punuoan)
Innovative medicines - CNS (XINYUE, Ameining, Ailanning, Oulanning)
Collaboration/out-licensing income (upfronts, milestones, royalties from GSK, Regeneron, Roche, Hengrui, Glenmark, Avere deals)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2C-via-hospital/pharmacy channel in China for product sales (national and provincial reimbursement-listed drugs), plus B2B licensing relationships with large global pharmaceutical/biotech partners for ex-China rights
business_model.geographic_mix: Revenue overwhelmingly generated in Mainland China; licensing deals monetize ex-China (US/EU/ROW) rights for self-developed assets while the Group retains China commercialization rights

main_competitors: Multinational originators (AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Merck) in NSCLC/oncology
competitive_position.market_position: One of China's largest innovation-driven pharmaceutical groups by R&D scale and a top-tier player in EGFR-TKI NSCLC (Ameile/aumolertinib) and in B7-H3/B7-H4-targeted ADCs (partnered with GSK); increasingly recognized internationally as a source of differentiated, licensable oncology and immunology assets

moat_factors.factor: Proprietary R&D platforms and pipeline depth
moat_factors.description: Over 2,300 researchers across 4 R&D centers (Shanghai, Changzhou, Lianyungang, Maryland US); 40+ innovative candidates in 70+ trials; proprietary PEGylation technology (Fulaimei) and ADC platform (HS-20093, HS-20089) validated by large pharma partners

Multiple high-value deals with GSK, Regeneron, Roche, Glenmark, Avere/NextCure and Hengrui provide third-party validation of asset quality and de-risk global commercialization without requiring Hansoh to build its own US/EU sales infrastructure

Multiple innovative medicines (Ameile, Hansoh Xinfu, XINYUE, Fulaimei, Hengmu, Saint Luolai) are included in and have been successfully renewed on the National Reimbursement Drug List, embedding products in China's standard-of-care pathways and hospital formularies

moat_factors.factor: Clinical evidence base and guideline inclusion
moat_factors.description: Ameile recommended as Class I/Preferred in 8 national guidelines; broad real-world evidence and phase III data (ARTS, AENEAS2, MITIGATE trials) support continued physician adoption and new indication approvals
Vertically integrated production (Jiangsu Hansoh) and decades of generics manufacturing experience provide a lower-cost base relative to multinational originators

weaknesses: Heavy revenue concentration in China (single-market regulatory, reimbursement and pricing exposure)
Product concentration risk: oncology (particularly Ameile/aumolertinib) is roughly two-thirds of revenue
Licensing/collaboration income is lumpy and milestone-contingent, making revenue mix harder to forecast
Dependent on continued NRDL renewal negotiations, which have historically required material price concessions
Smaller global commercial footprint than multinational originators; relies on partners (GSK, Roche, Regeneron, Avere) for ex-China commercialization rather than owning the full value chain

growth_drivers: Expanding indications for existing innovative medicines (Ameile now has 5 approved NSCLC indications; XINYUE expanding from NMOSD into IgG4-RD and gMG)
Maturing ADC pipeline (HS-20093/Risvutatug Rezetecan, HS-20089/Mocertatug Rezetecan) advancing into Phase III, partnered globally with GSK for upside beyond China

Accelerating out-licensing strategy: 2025-2026 deals with Regeneron (HS-20094 GLP-1/GIP), Roche (HS-20110 CDH17 ADC; October 2026 multi-asset ADC deal worth up to ~$15bn in milestones plus $400m upfront), Glenmark (aumolertinib ex-China territories, >$1bn potential), and Avere/NextCure (HS-20118 IL-23, ~$120m upfront + up to $2.18bn milestones, plus $320m equity stake)
Global regulatory expansion of aumolertinib (Aumseqa) via MHRA (UK) and EU approvals, opening new ex-China revenue avenues
Broader pipeline in GLP-1/GIP metabolic disease (weight management, diabetes) riding the global incretin growth wave

Favorable domestic policy tailwinds: China's 15th Five-Year Plan designates biopharma an 'emerging pillar industry'; April 2026 State Council opinion aims to improve first-launch pricing mechanisms for innovative drugs

Record industry-wide China out-licensing activity (China now ~50% of global licensing-deal value in 2025) validating the broader sector thesis and providing deal-market tailwinds for further Hansoh monetization

business.description: Highly competitive Chinese and global biopharma landscape; rivals (Hengrui, Innovent, BeiGene, CSPC, multinationals) could leapfrog with new technology platforms, eroding Hansoh's pipeline competitiveness
Long, costly, uncertain R&D cycles; candidates may fail to achieve expected clinical results, timely approval or commercial acceptance; patent disputes possible
Oncology products (led by Ameile) are ~66% of revenue; any competitive, safety, or reimbursement setback to key products would disproportionately affect results
Reliance on key R&D and management personnel in a highly competitive talent market for pharma scientists

financial.description: Upfront/milestone payments from licensing deals are lumpy and contingent on clinical/regulatory success by partners, making period-to-period collaboration revenue hard to predict
Assets/liabilities and licensing proceeds partly denominated in USD against RMB-reporting base; FX losses already appeared in FY2025 other expenses
R&D expenses grew faster than revenue in some periods (e.g., FY2025 R&D +24.3% vs revenue +22.6%), though currently well-funded by a strong net cash position (~RMB31.5bn cash at FY2025)

regulatory.risk: NRDL price negotiation / de facto volume-based procurement pressure
regulatory.description: National Reimbursement Drug List renewal negotiations have historically forced steep price cuts (averaging ~60% for newly negotiated oncology drugs industry-wide in recent rounds); continued inclusion is necessary for volume but each renewal risks further price erosion on products like Ameile, Hansoh Xinfu, XINYUE, Fulaimei, Hengmu and Saint Luolai

Evolving medical insurance and drug review/approval policy (NMPA, NHSA) could alter commercialization economics; company explicitly flags 'policies and regulations' as a principal risk given the fast-iterating Chinese regulatory environment

regulatory.risk: Cross-border biotech/geopolitical tension affecting licensing deals
regulatory.description: Hansoh's growth strategy increasingly depends on out-licensing IP to US/EU players (GSK, Regeneron, Roche, Avere); heightened US-China biotech scrutiny (e.g., potential restrictions on Chinese-origin biologics, national security reviews of licensing/investment deals, or shifts in US policy toward Chinese IP) could disrupt deal flow or valuations, though no deals have been blocked to date
Company-disclosed risk around data security, anti-corruption and anti-trust compliance across its global operations

macro.description: Reimbursement budgets and healthcare spending growth in China directly affect volume growth for NRDL-listed products

macro.risk: Global trade frictions and supply chain
macro.description: Company explicitly cites global trade frictions potentially affecting raw material costs, logistics costs and supply chain stability
USD-denominated licensing proceeds are subject to RMB/USD movements when translated into reporting currency

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's innovative pharmaceutical industry is transitioning from R&D-investment-driven growth to a 'quality and efficiency' model, with record 2025-2026 out-licensing deal volumes (China now ~50% of global pharma licensing transaction value) and government policy (15th Five-Year Plan naming biopharma an 'emerging pillar industry') providing strong tailwinds for globally competitive Chinese innovators like Hansoh
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate — pharmaceutical demand is largely non-discretionary and reimbursement-supported, but licensing/collaboration income is lumpy and deal-cycle dependent rather than steadily recurring
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity; large net cash position (~RMB31.5bn) means the company is a net beneficiary of higher rates via interest income, and has no meaningful debt-service burden
key_input_costs: Active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and raw materials

recent_developments.event: Entered a strategic collaboration and license agreement with Roche covering a portfolio of ADCs (including two Hansoh-originated programs); Hansoh to receive a $400 million upfront payment, a further $110 million at the one-year mark, milestone eligibility exceeding $15 billion in aggregate, plus tiered royalties

Signed exclusive global license agreement with Avere Therapeutics for HS-20118 (IL-23 receptor antagonist, ex-Greater China); Hansoh eligible for $120 million upfront and up to $2.18 billion in milestones; separately made a $320 million private placement into the Avere/NextCure combined entity, expected to hold 30-40% of the combined company

H1 2026 results: revenue RMB8,304 million (+11.7% YoY), profit RMB4,258 million (+35.8% YoY), EPS RMB0.70 (+33.1% YoY); innovative medicines revenue share rose to 85.4%; interim dividend of HK$28.50 cents per share declared
XINYUE (inebilizumab) granted NMPA approval for its third indication (generalized myasthenia gravis), expanding the product's addressable patient base in China
Aumolertinib (Ameile/Aumseqa) approved in the European Union as monotherapy for EGFR-mutated NSCLC, extending the drug's global regulatory footprint beyond the UK (MHRA, 2025) approval

Entered licensing deal with Glenmark for ex-China aumolertinib rights (Middle East/Africa, Southeast/South Asia, Australia, NZ, Russia/CIS, select Caribbean) with potential cumulative milestones over $1 billion plus tiered royalties; also licensed-in HS-10568 (CaSR modulator) from Hengrui for the PRC market
Entered exclusive worldwide (ex-Greater China/Taiwan) license agreement with Roche for HS-20110, an investigational CDH17-targeting ADC

Entered exclusive worldwide (ex-Greater China) license agreement with Regeneron for HS-20094, a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, positioning Hansoh in the global obesity/metabolic disease licensing wave

FY2025 results: revenue RMB15,028 million (+22.6% YoY), profit RMB5,555 million (+27.1% YoY); innovative medicines and collaborative products revenue reached ~82.2% of total revenue (first time exceeding 80%); completed three new overseas licensing collaborations in the year

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (June 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report

items.target: Continue to grow as a proportion of total revenue (currently ~85.4% in H1 2026, ~82.2% in FY2025)
items.notes: Management explicitly frames innovative medicines and collaboration income as the 'core driver for sustainable growth'; no specific numeric revenue or EPS target disclosed — guidance is qualitative/directional as is typical for the company

items.target: Continued year-on-year increase in R&D spend
items.notes: R&D expenses were ~20.9% of H1 2026 revenue (RMB1,739m, +20.7% YoY); company states it will keep increasing R&D investment to sustain pipeline competitiveness

items.target: Pursue further global out-licensing of pipeline assets to unlock ex-China value
items.notes: Prospects section cites robust industry-wide licensing activity (>1,000 global deals in 2025, ~$275bn disclosed value, China ~50% of transaction value) as context for continued deal pursuit; no specific deal-count or revenue target given

items.target: No disclosed material investment plans as of FY2025 year-end
items.notes: FY2025 annual report states the Group had no plans for material investments and capital assets as at December 31, 2025; FY2025 capex was RMB458-489 million, mainly workshop construction and equipment

guidance.management_commentary: Chairlady Zhong Huijuan (also CEO) emphasized that innovative medicines and collaborative products revenue exceeded 80% of total revenue for the first time in 2025, framing this as validation of the Group's 30-year innovation-driven strategy. Management highlighted three new overseas licensing collaborations completed in 2025 (extended further in H1-H2 2026 with Avere and Roche) as 'further optimizing our revenue mix,' and pointed to 'a broader innovation pipeline and several key products progressing into late-stage development and critical registration phases' as the basis for expecting future 'performance leap' from new product launches.

bull_case: Successful pivot from a generics-heavy, China-only pharma to a globally recognized innovative-drug platform, evidenced by validating deals with top-tier partners (GSK, Regeneron, Roche, Hengrui, Glenmark, Avere) and the October 2026 Roche ADC deal worth up to ~$15bn in potential milestones plus $400m upfront
Innovative medicines now ~85% of revenue and growing, with multiple products (Ameile, XINYUE, Fulaimei) still expanding indications and NRDL coverage, supporting a multi-year volume growth runway

Strong, growing ADC and GLP-1/GIP pipeline rides two of the hottest global biopharma themes (oncology ADCs, obesity/metabolic), de-risked by partnering with deep-pocketed multinationals for ex-China development/commercialization
Pristine balance sheet with ~RMB31.5bn net cash and low gearing (~11.4%) funds continued R&D investment and provides resilience/optionality without dilution or debt risk

Structural tailwind from Chinese government policy explicitly elevating biopharma to a national 'pillar industry' status and reforming drug pricing mechanisms to better reward first-launch innovative medicines
bear_case: Heavy reliance on China's National Reimbursement Drug List for product volumes exposes Hansoh to recurring, steep price-cut risk at each NRDL renewal cycle (historical average price reductions of ~60% for newly negotiated oncology drugs industry-wide)

Licensing/collaboration income, while a powerful upside driver, is lumpy, milestone-contingent and dependent on partners' (GSK, Roche, Regeneron, Avere) own clinical and regulatory success — meaningful risk that announced multi-billion-dollar milestone totals are not realized in full or on schedule

Revenue remains concentrated in a single national market (China) and in oncology (particularly aumolertinib/Ameile), leaving the company exposed to any adverse domestic regulatory, reimbursement or competitive shock

Intensifying competition from both domestic Chinese innovators (Hengrui, Innovent, BeiGene, CSPC, Junshi) and multinational originators in overlapping therapeutic areas (EGFR-TKI NSCLC, ADCs, GLP-1) could compress long-term pricing power and market share

Rising US-China biotech/geopolitical scrutiny could, in a tail-risk scenario, complicate or slow future out-licensing transactions to US/EU partners, an important and growing part of the forward growth and valuation thesis
